transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-20 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marco Li (Redwood SE), Priya Narang (Head of ML, Atlas), Carlos Mendez (Eng Mgr), Samir Patel (Infra)

Summary (auto): intro, qualification, architecture discussion, vector DB integration options, perf targets, security questions, next steps

[00:00] Jenna (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jenna with redwood inference, and this is marco our se. how's everyone doing?
[00:07] Priya (Atlas): good, thanks. excited to chat—we're trying to scope an embeddings + rerank pipeline and figure out whether hosted/dedicated/private makes sense.
[00:14] Marco (Redwood): great, can you give a bit of context on your current stack and what you want the rerank step to accomplish?
[00:20] Carlos (Atlas): yeah, currently we store docs in postgres + opensearch for text, and a separate vector store for embeddings. we experimented with pinecon—pinecone—sorry, pinecone—for smaller prod sets. our search flow today is bm25 then a cheap embedding similarity, then a cross-encoder rerank. latency is... kinda high for some use cases.
[00:36] Priya: target is sub-200ms p90 for user-facing search across a 10M+ corpus; internal analytics can tolerate higher. throughput target for API is about 200 qps for typical mix (mostly retrieval, ~20% heavy reranks).
[00:50] Marco: okay that clarifies a lot. couple things we'll want to size: embedding dimensionality (are you on 768 or 1536 or custom?), vector index choice (faiss/milvus/weaviate/pinecone), and whether you want redwood to host embeddings or keep vectors in your DB and call Redwood for embeddings + rerank only.
[01:05] Priya: right now embeddings are 1536 from an open model, but we may try 768 to reduce storage. tradeoffs there?
[01:12] Marco: yes—1536 gives better recall in many of our benchmarks, but costs and index memory go up linearly. you save both storage and some query time with 768. also depends on the vector index and quantization you plan to use. if you use IVF+SQ8 in faiss, 1536 with quantization still works but CPU/GPU memory hit differs.
[01:30] Carlos: talk to me about hybrid search—our PM wants bm25 + embeddings + rerank. is that a pattern redwood supports?
[01:37] Jenna: absolutely; most customers run a hybrid flow: bm25 to cheaply narrow candidates, then dense retrieval for recall, then a cross-encoder or light transformer for rerank. Redwood can host the models for embedding + rerank, and you can keep vectors in your DB or use our managed vector store.
[01:52] Samir (Infra): on the infra side we care about VPC/VPN, KMS, and data residency. If we go private, we need HSM/KMS integration and audit logs. SOC2 is also required.
[02:02] Marco: we support private deployments with a customer-controlled control plane and KMS integrations. our audit logs and traces are part of Redwood Console; SOC2 Type II is available and we can share the attestation. for HSM we integrate with common cloud KMS providers; on-prem HSMs are possible in private.
[02:20] Priya: great. how do dedicated GPU pools help for rerank? we expect the cross-encoder to be heavier per-query.
[02:27] Marco: dedicated pools give predictable throughput—if you lock capacity you get guaranteed qps and lower variance. cross-encoders are expensive: think 20-60ms on a good GPU for a single pass depending on model size and sequence length. for a 200 qps peak with 20% rerank, you'll need to size accordingly or run batching. Redwood's runtime supports batching and auto batchers that keep latency SLOs.
[02:46] Carlos: do you support per-request routing? e.g., route low-priority analytic searches to cheaper hardware?
[02:51] Jenna: yes, we have smart routing policies—route by latency SLO, customer tier, region. fallback to a cheaper model variant is possible if high tier capacity is saturated.
[02:59] Priya: what's the latency when using an external vector DB like milvus vs using redwood's managed store?
[03:04] Marco: raw vector lookup is usually network and index dependent. with a co-located store (same VPC) you'd see sub-10ms for ANN lookups at small k; across network maybe 20-40ms. Redwood's managed vector store co-located with the runtime reduces network hops. if you keep vectors in your DB, we recommend colocating or using fast private peering.
[03:27] Priya: and how about dimensionality impact on throughput—if we drop to 768 does qps improve much?
[03:32] Marco: index search time reduces, memory footprint roughly halves, so batch throughput increases. but rerank stage cost is model-dependent (token length), not embed dimension. however increased candidate set from cheaper embeddings can increase rerank load.
[03:46] Carlos: any guidance on the routing between bm25 and dense? e.g., top 100 from bm25 then dense rerank?
[03:51] Marco: common approach is retrieve top N (100-500) with BM25, dedupe, then dense similarity to pick top K (50-200) to send to cross-encoder rerank. tradeoff is recall vs latency/cost. we can help tune N/K given your SLOs.
[04:10] Priya: what about memory limits—our infra team tends to prefer quantized indexes to reduce RAM; are there recommendations?
[04:17] Marco: yes PQ/SQ8/INT8 quantization is common. Redwood's recommendations depend on model/quality tradeoffs; we can run a sweep. Dedicated allows using GPU-resident indexes for fast ANN and heavier rerank. Private deployment gives you full control for on-prem index choices.
[04:33] Jenna: quick question—are you expecting to persist embeddings in our managed store or in your existing vector DB?
[04:38] Priya: preference is to keep control of vectors in our existing DB for compliance, but we might pilot with Redwood's managed store for the POC.
[04:46] Marco: that works—pilot with managed store simplifies benchmarking; then move to customer-managed store with private peering for production.
[04:53] Samir: security checklist—SSO (SAML), RBAC, audit logs, KMS e2e, SOC2. will you be able to provide architecture docs for private deployment?
[05:02] Jenna: yes we'll share security docs and our SOC2 report. for SAML/SSO we support SAML 2.0 and OIDC, and RBAC can be scoped by team/route.
[05:11] Carlos: curious about pricing—how is dedicated priced vs hosted?
[05:15] Jenna: hosted is usage-based (per-token / per-embedding unit). Dedicated is capacity/reserved monthly commit with lower unit cost and guaranteed throughput. Private has platform fees plus support. we'll send an initial pricing sheet tailored to your throughput/embedding dims and storage needs.
[05:30] Priya: for the POC we'd like Redwood to run a 100k vector benchmark with our sample and show latency/% recall differences between 768/1536 and shared vs dedicated setups. can you do that?
[05:40] Marco: yes, we can run those benchmarks. we'll need the sample dataset and expected queries. we'll also want to instrument a few eval prompts to measure rerank quality (MRR, NDCG).
[05:51] Priya: what's the easiest way to share data securely?
[05:54] Samir: we can S3 presigned, or if private deployment we can do a peered transfer. we'll prefer S3 presigned for the POC.
[06:00] Jenna: works for us—please include a small README with the vector format, dims, and typical query set.
[06:06] Carlos: any gotchas around tokenization mismatch for rerank models? we've seen inconsistent tokenizations when models differ for retrieval vs rerank.
[06:14] Marco: good point—ensure consistent text normalization, and if possible use the same tokenizer family or map tokens. we often recommend using the same embedding model family as the reranker or include a lightweight normalization step. small differences can cause rerank mismatch.
[06:29] Priya: regarding compliance, do you support data residency? some EU user data must stay in eu regions.
[06:36] Jenna: yes, we support region pinning and can run private control planes in-region. we'll note that some private/on-prem options are best for strict residency.
[06:45] Carlos: for the cross-encoder—are you suggesting a smaller transformer or something like a 3B parameter model?
[06:51] Marco: depends on quality/latency tradeoff. 1-3B models are common for good rerank quality while keeping latency in check. larger models give small gains but incur big latency/cost. some customers use smaller cross-encoders with distillation.
[07:06] Priya: ok that makes sense. curious about caching—do you support prefix or KV cache to speed repeated queries?
[07:12] Marco: yes we have automatic KV/prefix caching for recent prompts and rerank results; this can dramatically reduce cost for repeat queries.
[07:20] Jenna: quick recap of what we heard: 1) goal: sub-200ms p90 user search across 10M+ docs, 200 qps mix with 20% rerank. 2) current: 1536 dims, open model embeddings, storing vectors in customer DB. 3) security: SOC2, SAML, KMS, region pinning required. 4) ask: POC for 100k sample + benchmarks for 768 vs 1536 and managed vs customer-managed store.
[07:45] Priya: yep that sums it up. any blockers on your side?
[07:49] Marco: no blockers. we'll need the sample and will prepare a perf checklist.
[07:54] Jenna: action items: i'll send pricing and benchmark template; marco will prepare perf checklist; priya will share sample dataset via presigned s3.
[08:03] Carlos: timeline—we want POC within 2-3 weeks, then decide on dedicated or private in 4-6 weeks depending on results.
[08:11] Jenna: sounds reasonable. we'll aim to have the benchmark results within 10 business days of receiving the sample.
[08:18] Priya: any recommended metrics we should look at for rerank quality?
[08:21] Marco: MRR, NDCG@10, recall@K, and p90/p95 latency for end-to-end flow. also track cost per query.
[08:31] Jenna: i'll share our benchmark sheet and security docs after the call.
[08:35] Samir: we'll also need a network diagram for private deployment; can you include connectivity patterns?
[08:40] Marco: yes we'll include VPC peering, private peering, and on-prem options in the doc.
[08:46] Priya: ok thanks everyone.
[08:49] Jenna: thanks all. next steps recap in the calendar invite and i'll follow up with docs & pricing.
[08:54] Priya: thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
